sections.overview: Scinax flavoguttatus is a frog of Brazil’s Atlantic Forest region, recorded from coastal and nearby mountain areas.
sections.identification: Its common name is Yellowbelly Snouted Treefrog; the species has been studied as a distinct member of the Scinax catharinae group.
sections.habitat: Field observations associate it with forested streams, where adults perch on leaves or roots near the water.
sections.diet: The sources consulted do not provide a reliable species-specific account of adult feeding.
sections.behavior: Males have been observed calling from streamside vegetation, sometimes close to other calling males.
sections.reproduction: Eggs are deposited in calm sections of streams, and tadpoles use flowing-water habitats.
sections.ecology: Current Amphibian Species of the World treatment uses the name Ololygon flavoguttata; this profile retains the catalogue name and ID Scinax flavoguttatus.
sections.conservation: An older IUCN assessment lists the species as Least Concern and notes habitat loss as a concern; the assessment is not a current population estimate.
